elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly includes Customer's “Affiliates.” The direct written grant also constitutes specific contractual authorization notwithstanding paragraph (a)'s restriction on unauthorized third-party access.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly includes “contractors acting on Customer's behalf.”

elements.element: A paid-up licence, if any, has perpetual duration.
elements.evidence: The clause grants a royalty-free licence to a hosted platform as part of the Services and ties its duration to the Agreement; it does not establish any paid-up licence. The condition is therefore demonstrably absent from the supplied language.

elements.element: A paid-up licence, if any, is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No paid-up licence is established in the supplied language; the only licence shown is a royalty-free, Agreement-linked hosted-service licence. The condition is therefore demonstrably absent.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for Customer's material breach.
elements.evidence: The licence is revocable upon expiration or any termination of the Agreement under paragraph 4. Paragraph 4 is not supplied, and the operative language does not restrict termination to Customer's material breach.

elements.element: The material breach must remain uncured when a subscription licence is terminated.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no uncured-breach requirement or cure condition.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to successors.
elements.evidence: The grant is expressly “transferable to a successor in accordance with the assignment provisions,” and paragraph (h) permits assignment to purchasers of substantially all relevant assets and successors through merger, stock sale, consolidation, or similar transactions.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are eligible for licence coverage.
elements.evidence: Customer's Affiliates are direct licensees under the rendered grant.

elements.element: Customer can obtain affiliate coverage by written notice to Kubient, without requiring Kubient's consent.
elements.evidence: The rendered grant covers Affiliates automatically, without either notice or consent. This is broader than, and therefore satisfies, a right to obtain coverage merely by written notice.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The licence is transferable under paragraph (h), which expressly permits no-consent assignment to a purchaser of substantially all relevant assets or a successor by merger, stock sale, consolidation, or similar transaction.

result.reason: The redline fully reaches the fallback and adds the requested affiliate, contractor, and successor coverage. It does not reach the preferred subscription position because expiration or termination under paragraph 4 remains sufficient, with no express material-breach or uncured-breach limitation. It is also not minimal: deleting the express prohibition on sublicensing was unnecessary to make Affiliates and contractors direct licensees and may broaden the licence beyond the requested positions. The phrase “revocable only upon expiration” is conceptually awkward, and the termination cross-reference leaves the operative standard uncertain, although no contradiction with the retained assignment or third-party-access provisions is necessarily introduced.
